prompt: Build the routing table of a small web framework: register path patterns with {placeholders} and match an incoming path, capturing the placeholder values. Complete add and match.
explanation: Routing is segment-by-segment comparison: split both the pattern and the incoming path on '/', require the same number of segments, then compare literals for equality and treat any {name} segment as a wildcard that records its value. Normalising a trailing slash before splitting means /users/42 and /users/42/ are the same route, which is what users expect. Trying the patterns in registration order makes the behaviour predictable -- first match wins, so a specific route must be registered before a more general one that would also match it.
hints: Write a small helper that strips a trailing '/' and returns path.split("/", -1); use it on both the pattern and the incoming path so they are compared the same way.
A segment is a placeholder when it startsWith("{") and endsWith("}"); the parameter name is the text between the braces.
Collect parameters into a fresh map for each candidate pattern, and only return a RouteMatch once every segment has matched -- a half-filled map from a failed candidate must not leak into the result.
